question: Is this project allowed to publish or trade NBA-derived lines at all?
known: The model consumes nba.com statistics and official injury reports. NBA Terms of Use section 9 restricts gambling use of NBA Statistics. Dutch rules require a Koa licence to offer online sports betting to residents of the Netherlands.
missing: A legal decision, and confirmation of the jurisdictions the site will serve.
next_step: Owner picks a jurisdiction set and asks a lawyer to read NBA Terms of Use section 9 and the Dutch Betting and Gaming Act article 31a before anything is published to end users.

question: Where does the price come from if no bookmaker price is available?
known: Every line here is originated by this project (spread, total, fair moneyline). No licensed odds feed is connected and no market comparison has been performed, so no ROI, no market edge and no de-vigging exist in this repository.
missing: A licensed odds feed, and a decision on whether the project stays a paper research system.
next_step: Owner decides: connect a licensed feed, or keep the system research-only and publish fair prices with no expected value.

question: How many games does a strategy need before it can be called skill?
known: Seven gates are defined. The two strongest signals rest on 24 and 28 observations (21/24 and 20/28). The minimum-sample gate of 100 is not met, and the observed effects are under-powered: S4b needs about 76 more games to reach 80% power.
missing: More seasons of data, and an agreed minimum observation count for a promoted strategy.
next_step: Re-run the same gates after roughly 100 further games and publish the power calculation for each strategy.

question: Can the totals side of the book be used at all?
known: Walk-forward RMSE for the total is 20.35 against a 19.56 league-average baseline, so the totals model is worse than doing nothing. The margin model improves on its baseline (16.18 vs 17.30).
missing: A totals model that beats the baseline.
next_step: Rebuild the totals model on possession and pace inputs, then re-run the same walk-forward test.

question: What is the real home-court advantage in 2026-27?
known: Least squares on 174 verified results gives +1.59 points with a two-sided p of 0.104 and 172 degrees of freedom, so this sample does not establish it.
missing: A season-long estimate, and a decision on whether to use the fitted value or a published prior.
next_step: Recompute after the season sample grows and compare with the league's own home record.

question: Which injuries actually move the line, and by how much?
known: 117 player rows are available from the official report, and minutes-at-risk is quantified where the player's season minutes per game are in the captured top-31 set. Six players are quantified with their official minutes; the rest are blank.
missing: Per-player game logs, a replacement-player model, and the elasticity of team rating to minutes. The current impact is a minutes count, not a points estimate.
next_step: Capture per-player box scores and fit a minutes-to-rating model; until then no points impact is published.

question: How correlated are player props in the same game?
known: Team-level and game-level correlations are measured (home points vs away points r = 0.128, n = 174; spread residual vs total residual r = 0.091, n = 114; cover-and-over phi = 0.109, n = 114). Player-level correlations are blank.
missing: Per-player game logs, which were never captured.
next_step: Pull nba.com/stats player box scores for two seasons and compute the same-game player correlation matrix with confidence intervals.

question: Are the player-prop lines published here real lines or projections?
known: The prop table carries official season averages and a pro-rata minutes redistribution assumption. It explicitly states the over/under distribution is not established and marks every line as unverified.
missing: A verified prop line feed and a projected-minutes model.
next_step: Owner decides whether to keep publishing projections with the caveat, or to suppress the prop page until a real feed exists.

question: Which injury report should be canonical when two versions of the same report exist?
known: The 11/13 07:30 PM report (used here, 117 player rows fully attributed) and the 11/13 05:00 PM report (used by the /site/ tree, 18 rows unattributed) disagree on 12 statuses.
missing: A rule that says which snapshot is authoritative and that every tree obeys it.
next_step: Owner names one snapshot per slate and the older trees are either regenerated or retired.

question: Are the 174 results in the training log correct?
status: answered for the aggregate, open per game
known: 348 team-games reconcile exactly against the official games-played column for all 30 teams (mismatch 0), and the official W-L columns match the recomputed records. 81 of the overlapping injury rows also match the earlier independent transcription.
missing: A per-game check of all 174 results against official box scores.
next_step: Pull nba.com box scores for the 174 games and diff every score line.

question: How are the seven existing site trees related, and which one is authoritative?
known: Seven trees exist with incompatible ID namespaces and partly different data snapshots. This dashboard consolidates them and states which artifact each number comes from.
missing: A decision to retire the older trees, keep them as archives, or keep them live.
next_step: Owner decides; then this dashboard becomes the only live tree and the others are archived.

question: What is the stake plan and the stop rule?
known: Nothing in the repository defines stake sizing, bankroll, drawdown limits or a stop rule.
next_step: Owner sets a bankroll and a flat or fractional stake rule before any strategy is traded on paper.

question: Can the system roll forward to the next slate without a manual run?
known: The picks generator hard codes 2026-11-14 to 2026-11-16, so it does not advance by itself.
missing: A scheduler and a window that is derived from the official schedule.
next_step: Derive the window from the official schedule at run time and add a scheduled job.

question: Is the model's edge skill or luck?
known: Margin variance explained is 12.5% and total variance explained is -8.2%. The two best strategies pass the raw-p and false-discovery gates but fail on sample size. That is the signature of an under-powered result, not a demonstrated edge.
missing: A larger sample and a pre-registered strategy list so that the surviving strategy is not one of many that were tried.
next_step: Freeze the strategy list now, then re-test the frozen list after 100 further games.

question: What would the picks be worth at a real price?
known: The project publishes fair moneylines derived from its own model probabilities for every game in the window.
missing: Any market price to compare them with, so expected value, edge and hold-adjusted numbers stay blank.
next_step: Same as Q-02: a licensed odds feed, or a decision to publish fair prices only.

question: Is the three-day window the right horizon?
known: The brief sets a maximum of three days ahead and the system covers 2026-11-13 to 2026-11-16 (31 games).
missing: A decision on whether the horizon should shrink as report coverage improves, since injury reports for 11/15 and 11/16 do not exist yet.
next_step: Owner confirms the horizon; the generator should then derive it from the schedule.
